name_en: Keiran — sweet red-bean mochi dumplings in a clear soy broth
summary_ja: もち米粉の生地でこしあんを包み、卵形に整えてしいたけと昆布の澄まし汁に浮かべる。形が鶏卵に似ることから名がついたと伝わり、稲刈り後の「秋仕舞い」のもてなし料理として下北地方に受け継がれている。
summary_en: Two egg-shaped mochi dumplings filled with sweet red-bean paste float in a clear shiitake-kelp broth, said to be named for their resemblance to hen's eggs and served at Shimokita's post-harvest gatherings.

name_en: Keno jiru — a slow-simmered New Year root vegetable and bean soup
summary_ja: 大根やごぼう、わらびなど根菜と山菜をさいの目に刻み、すりつぶした大豆とともに焼き干し出汁で煮込む。小正月に大鍋で仕込み、数日かけて温め直しながら食べる津軽地方の保存食である。
summary_en: Diced daikon, burdock and fern shoots simmered with mashed soybeans in a smoky dried-fish broth — a Tsugaru dish traditionally made in a big pot for the Little New Year and reheated over several days.

name_en: Senbei jiru — a soy-flavored hotpot with hard wheat crackers simmered soft
summary_ja: 南部せんべいを鶏だし醤油の鍋に割り入れ、ごぼうや凍み豆腐と煮込む。冷害で米が実りにくかった八戸で保存食のせんべいを鍋に使ったのが始まりとされ、汁を吸ってもちもちした食感が特徴。
summary_en: Hard wheat crackers are broken into a chicken-and-soy broth with burdock and freeze-dried tofu until chewy — born in Hachinohe, where the crackers were a famine-proof staple long before they became hotpot fare.
source_title: せんべい汁 青森県

name_en: Jappa jiru — a whole-fish cod soup made from the parts usually discarded
summary_ja: 「じゃっぱ」は津軽の方言で本来捨てる部位を指し、タラの頭や骨、内臓を大根やねぎと煮込む。正月にタラを一尾丸ごと買う風習があった津軽で、冬の漁から戻った体を温める汁として親しまれた。
summary_en: "Jappa" means the cod parts usually thrown away — head, bones, innards — simmered with daikon and scallion, a warming winter soup from Tsugaru, where buying a whole cod for New Year was once the custom.
source_title: 鱈のじゃっぱ汁 青森県

name_en: Ichigoni — a delicate sea urchin and abalone clear soup
summary_ja: 生ウニとアワビを水かだしでさっと煮て醤油少々で整え、青じそを添えるだけの潮の香り豊かな吸い物。乳白色の汁に浮くウニが野いちごのように見えることが名の由来とされ、祝い事の椀に用いられる。
summary_en: Fresh sea urchin and abalone are barely simmered in dashi with a touch of soy sauce and shiso — the golden urchin adrift in the pale broth is said to resemble wild strawberries, hence the name, served at celebrations.

name_en: Hittsumi — hand-torn wheat dough simmered in a chicken and root vegetable soup
summary_ja: こねた小麦粉の生地を手でちぎって鶏だし醤油の汁に入れ、人参やごぼうとともに煮込む。旧南部藩領だった青森県南東部から岩手県北中部にかけて伝わり、米が不作の年の主食代わりとされた。
summary_en: Hand-torn pieces of kneaded wheat dough are simmered in a chicken-and-soy broth with carrot and burdock — a dish from the old Nanbu domain spanning southeastern Aomori and northern Iwate, once a rice substitute in lean years.

name_en: Shoga miso oden — oden served with a grated ginger and red miso sauce
summary_ja: 煮たおでんに、赤味噌とみりん、だしを煮立てすりおろし生姜を混ぜたたれをかけて食べる。戦後の青函連絡船の屋台で客の体を温めようと出したのが始まりと伝わり、つぶ貝や大ぶりの練り物が具に入る。
summary_en: Simmered oden is topped with a sauce of red miso, mirin, dashi and grated ginger — said to have begun at a postwar street stall warming travelers bound for the Aomori-Hakodate ferry, served with local whelk and oversized fish cakes.
source_title: しょうが味噌おでん 青森県

name_en: Kujira jiru — a hearty New Year soup of salted whale blubber and root vegetables
summary_ja: 塩漬けにしたクジラの脂身を湯通しして脂を落とし、大根や人参、じゃがいもとともに大鍋で煮込む。捕鯨基地があった八戸周辺に伝わる正月料理で、日を経るごとに味がなじむとされる。
summary_en: Salted whale blubber is parboiled to render off excess fat, then simmered in a big pot with daikon, carrot and potato — a New Year dish from around Hachinohe's old whaling grounds, said to deepen in flavor over several days.
